        "title": "ARC: stamp a compact pattern at scattered markers",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background, one compact source pattern, and scattered single-cell markers, consider a pattern-stamping rule when demonstrations support it. Preserve the source pattern and replace each isolated marker by stamping the source's non-background cells centered on that marker, in the same orientation. Treat source-background cells as transparent and keep grid dimensions fixed. Clip stamps at grid boundaries if necessary; if stamps overlap, apply the pattern consistently while preserving non-background cells. In a verified task, this rule used a centered 3×3 source pattern and solved correctly. Check demonstrations for anchor alignment and any boundary or overlap cases before relying on those behaviors.",

      "arc_connect_collinear_markers_rows_columns": {
        "id": "arc_connect_collinear_markers_rows_columns",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: connect collinear markers with careful interval boundaries",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background and scattered markers of one color, inspect each row and column independently. When a line contains at least two markers, fill every background cell strictly between the outermost markers with color 3; equivalently, fill the intervals between consecutive markers. Preserve the marker cells and all cells outside those intervals. Check indexing carefully: between positions a and b, fill a+1 through b-1, never the endpoints. For example, markers at rows 1 and 4 require filling rows 2 and 3. Apply only when demonstrations support this rule, and preserve dimensions.",

      "arc_aligned_panels_shared_color_overlap": {
        "id": "arc_aligned_panels_shared_color_overlap",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: mark shared-color overlaps in aligned panels",
        "content": "For ARC grids divided into two aligned panels by a single-color separator, first confirm the separator orientation and that the panels have matching dimensions. Determine which color occurs in both panel palettes; do not assume it is the most frequent color. Create an output with the shared color as the background, and place color 3 at each corresponding position where both panels contain that shared color. Preserve panel alignment when comparing cells. This rule was validated on three demonstrations and successful tasks. Additional validation: task-14326ef7 had a 19×21 input with a color-8 vertical divider at column 10, forming aligned 19×10 panels. Their sole shared palette color was 4. The correct output omitted the divider, used 4 as background, and placed 3 at matching local coordinates (1,2), (3,6), (5,3), and (16,2), using zero-based indexing.",

      "arc_recolor_background_and_markers_using_a_demonstrated_color_map": {
        "id": "arc_recolor_background_and_markers_using_a_demonstrated_color_map",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: recolor background and markers using a demonstrated color map",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background and scattered single-cell markers of another color, consider a whole-grid recoloring rule when a demonstration supports it: map every background cell to the marker color and every marker cell to 0. Infer the exact mapping from the input-output pair, then apply it to every cell and preserve grid dimensions. Do not connect markers or otherwise alter their positions unless demonstrations show that behavior. Evidence: an input using colors 5 (background) and 4 (markers) produced 4 (former background) and 0 (former markers); applying the same mapping to a test with colors 5 and 9 solved it. If the rule is ambiguous, request a demonstration rather than assuming a geometric marker rule.",

        "content": "For ARC grids with noisy background cells and a compact colored object/polyomino, consider using the object's exact cell shape as a template when demonstrations support it. Enumerate every valid translation of the template and accept a match only when every template cell overlays the designated background color. Recolor the matched template cells to the object's color; preserve the source object and all other cells, and keep dimensions unchanged.         "content": "For ARC grids with a full horizontal or vertical color-2 stripe and a separate compact object or run on a uniform background, consider the demonstrated relocation rule. Move the object, preserving its shape and color, to become immediately adjacent to the stripe on the object's side of it. Paint the next full row or column beyond the relocated object, away from the stripe, color 8. Clear the object's original cells to the background; preserve the stripe and unrelated cells. Infer orientation and side from the input, and use demonstrations to verify the relocation and trail placement.",

      "arc_complete_a_partially_shown_periodic_grid_pattern": {
        "id": "arc_complete_a_partially_shown_periodic_grid_pattern",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: complete a partially shown periodic grid pattern",
        "content": "When an ARC grid contains a partial repeating color pattern, infer the shortest demonstrated period and extend it across the blank cells while preserving the grid size. For horizontal full-width bands, read the known row colors as an ordered sequence and continue that sequence in both directions, anchored to the existing rows. Evidence: a 4x4 grid with rows [3,9,9,blank] completed as [3,9,9,3] (period 3); a 16x16 grid with bottom rows 1,9,6 completed as the repeating row cycle 6,1,9 from the top (period 3); and a 5x5 grid with known rows 1=9 and 2=4 completed as rows 0..4 = 4,9,4,9,4 (period 2). Do not assume a row-reflection or repeat the observed sequence only once. Other demos in the same task showed analogous cyclic completion along diagonals, so inspect the geometry of the existing repeated pattern before choosing the axis.",

      "arc_periodic_grid_completion_partial_pattern_task0737": {
        "id": "arc_periodic_grid_completion_partial_pattern_task0737",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC periodic-grid completion from partial pattern",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a partial repeating pattern, infer the shortest period consistent with the known cells and extend it through blanks, anchored to known cells and preserving dimensions. First identify the pattern orientation. For full-width horizontal bands, represent the nonzero row colors as constraints on a vertical cycle: for a candidate period p, rows with the same index modulo p must have the same known color. Choose the smallest p satisfying all constraints, then assign each residue its anchored color and repeat the cycle in both directions. This handles sparse as well as contiguous bands. Example: known rows r=3:4, r=5:7, r=10:6 (0-based) conflict for p=1 and p=2; shortest valid period is p=3, fixing residues r mod 3 as 0->4, 1->6, 2->7, so the entire grid is filled with uniform rows cycling 4,6,7. If some residues remain unanchored, the period alone does not specify their colors; seek more evidence rather than inventing colors. Earlier examples: [3,9,9,blank] completed to [3,9,9,3] (period 3); known bottom rows 1,9,6 in a 16x16 grid extended upward as the 6,1,9 cycle; known rows 1=9 and 2=4 in a 5-row grid yielded 4,9,4,9,4 (period 2). Do not assume reflection or only copy once. Other examples in this task showed cyclic completion along diagonals, so identify orientation before applying a row-cycle rule.",

Verify compartment dimensions, divider positions, source alignment, and which cells are background before applying the rule. Preserve divider lines, dimensions, and the pattern's alignment within each compartment. Recolor only the matched template cells to the seed color. Keep the template in exactly its original orientation: do not rotate or reflect it. Infer the permitted gap length, alignment, and any group-size conditions from the demonstrations; do not automatically connect every collinear pair or draw a complete bounding-box frame.       "arc_stamp_exact_orientation_copies_of_a_colored_seed_onto_zero_matches": {
        "id": "arc_stamp_exact_orientation_copies_of_a_colored_seed_onto_zero_matches",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: stamp exact-orientation copies of a colored seed onto zero matches",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a distinctive small object in a non-background color amid zeros and background, use the seed object’s exact cell offsets as a template. Scan translations in the same orientation; when every template cell lands on 0, recolor those cells with the seed color. Preserve all other cells, including the seed, nonzero blockers, and zeros not covered by a valid placement. Overlapping valid placements are allowed; color the union of their template cells. Evidence: task-e526bee5 had a 3-cell L seed (top-right plus both cells below); its demo had a 5-cell seed and showed exact-orientation copies marked in zero regions while nonzero blockers prevented a match. Applying all valid all-zero placements solved the test correctly. This is also consistent with the related memory arc_find_and_recolor_exact_template_copies_in_noisy_grids.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: overlay aligned binary panels and mark their intersection",
        "content": "For ARC grids split into two same-sized binary panels by a vertical separator, a demonstration may define an aligned cellwise intersection: emit the output marker only where both corresponding panel cells are non-background; otherwise emit background. Remove the separator and return a grid with the panels' shared height and width. Infer output marker/background colors from demonstrations rather than assuming them. Evidence: a demo with left marker 3, right marker 8, separator 6 produced marker 2 exactly where left and right both had markers. A test with left marker 5, right marker 6 with holes 0, separator 8 had output 2 at shared nonzero locations and 0 elsewhere. Carefully align same row/column indices: the right panel begins immediately after the separator. On this instance, first submission missed an overlap because it misread the first right-panel cell; corrected submission was accepted.",

        "title": "ARC: mask foreground cells with aligned background panel",
        "content": "For ARC grids split into two equal-sized panels by a one-cell divider, the right panel can act as a mask over the left. Demonstrations may show an output the size of one panel: place the demonstrated output marker (here color 2) where the left cell is the foreground color AND the aligned right-panel cell is the panel background color; output 0 otherwise. In the example, left foreground 6 was retained only when aligned right cell was 3 (right-panel zeros removed those positions). In the test, left foreground 3 was retained only when aligned right cell was 9 (right-panel zeros removed positions). Keep row/column alignment and do not include the divider. Preserve the divider and the original populated band.       "arc_mark_compartments_containing_repeated_anomaly_cells": {
        "id": "arc_mark_compartments_containing_repeated_anomaly_cells",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: mark compartments containing repeated anomaly cells",
        "content": "For ARC grids partitioned by full-width horizontal divider rows and full-height vertical divider columns, treat each resulting equal-sized compartment as one output cell when demonstrations support it. If a compartment is mostly a uniform background color with isolated cells of another color, count the isolated anomaly cells in each compartment. The demonstrated rule here outputs a compact matrix with one cell per compartment: use the original background color as the output background, and place marker color 1 at the position of any compartment containing exactly two anomaly cells; compartments with zero or one anomaly stay background. Demonstration: a 19x11 grid had four 4x2 compartment rows and four 2-wide compartment columns (separators color 5); anomalous color 0 appeared in each block, and only block (row-band 1, column-block 3) had two anomalies, so output was 4x4 of color 2 with a 1 at output [1][3]. In the solved 19x5 test, separators color 3 made four bands and two columns; color 5 occurred twice in blocks [1][1] and [2][1], yielding a 4x2 output with those two cells marked 1 and all others background 7. Infer marker/count rule from demos rather than assuming the threshold for new tasks.",

        "title": "ARC: project marker rays between offset parallel border segments",
        "content": "For ARC grids where demonstrations show two equal-length, parallel, offset border segments and special-color markers, consider a projection rule. Infer which segment corresponds to each marker and how offsets map from the demonstrations; do not assume a fixed orientation or direction. Recolor each special marker to 4, extend its original marker color along the perpendicular ray toward its associated border, and draw the demonstrated full perpendicular line at the corresponding offset on the other segment. Preserve border cells and unrelated cells. Check the complete span and endpoints of every projected line: a line may extend across the grid to an edge where no border segment is present. Validate marker recoloring, segment-relative coordinate mapping, ray direction, and line endpoints against the examples before applying the rule.",

        "content": "When an ARC grid has two equal-sized panels separated by a solid one-cell divider, align corresponding cells and, when demonstrations support intersection, output one panel-sized grid. Write the demonstrated output marker where both panel cells are foreground (nonzero), and 0 elsewhere; omit the divider. Foreground colors need not match each other or the divider color: a verified case used panel colors 5 and 7 with divider 4 in the demo, and panel colors 8 and 6 with divider 1 in the test, producing marker color 2 exactly at cellwise nonzero intersections.       "arc_scale_grid_to_three_times_height_and_twice_width_with_copy_reflection_behavi": {
        "id": "arc_scale_grid_to_three_times_height_and_twice_width_with_copy_reflection_behavi",
        "kind": "memory",
